detail.title: Justice Decision Observability™ (JDO™) The Explainability Gap: Why Institutions Can Explain Systems, Policies, and Outcomes—but Still Cannot Explain Decisions
detail.abstract:
As artificial intelligence and decision-support technologies become increasingly integrated into justice environments, institutions face growing expectations regarding transparency, accountability, and explainability. Existing governance frameworks often focus on explaining system performance, regulatory compliance, risk management, security controls, and institutional outcomes. While these forms of explainability are important, they may leave a critical question insufficiently addressed: how a consequential decision actually formed.

This publication introduces the concept of the Explainability Gap — the difference between an institution’s ability to explain systems, policies, procedures, and outcomes, and its ability to explain the decision formation process connecting them. The paper argues that organizations frequently possess substantial visibility into what happened while possessing comparatively limited visibility into how judgment, interpretation, authority, and operational conditions shaped institutional action.

The publication further argues that decision explainability represents a distinct governance challenge that cannot be fully addressed through model explainability, compliance documentation, audit activities, or outcome review alone. Justice Decision Observability™ (JDO™) is introduced as a governance discipline focused on improving visibility into decision formation within AI-supported justice environments.

This publication is conceptual and doctrinal in nature and intentionally excludes operational methodologies, reconstruction procedures, implementation frameworks, analytical models, scoring systems, governance instrumentation mechanisms, and proprietary Justice Beacon Solutions™ operational structures.

title: MIVL: A Memory Integrity Verification Layer for Detecting and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks in Agentic AI Systems

detail.title: MIVL: A Memory Integrity Verification Layer for Detecting and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks in Agentic AI Systems

detail.abstract: Agentic AI systems that maintain persistent memory across sessions are vulnerable to memory poisoning attacks, in which adversaries plant malicious entries that silently alter long-term agent behaviour. Existing defences target single-turn prompt injection and do not address the persistence, gradual accumulation, or cross-agent propagation vectors that threaten multi-session agents. We present MIVL (Memory Integrity Verification Layer), a five-signal detection pipeline that computes a Memory Integrity Score (MIS) for every candidate memory write before it is committed. The five signals are: Semantic Intent Drift Detection (S1-SIDD), Command/Instruction Vocabulary Score (S2-CIVS), Temporal Drift Monitor (S3-TDM), Provenance Verification Score (S4-PVS), and Cross-Context Contradiction Ratio (S5-CCCR). A tiered remediation system routes flagged writes to one of five actions: BLOCK, QUARANTINE, SANITIZE, FLAG, or ROLLBACK. Evaluated on a labelled dataset of 200 memory write examples spanning four attack classes, MIVL achieves F1 = 0.8804, AUROC = 0.9023, and a false positive rate of 3.0% at the default threshold T M = 0.30. All five Gemini Memory Attack variants are successfully detected. The dataset and implementation are open-sourced.

title: Responsibility Vacuum in agent Skill Ecosystems: An Exploratory Anticipatory Governance Framework from the Pacing Problem Perspective Authors

detail.title: Responsibility Vacuum in agent Skill Ecosystems: An Exploratory Anticipatory Governance Framework from the Pacing Problem Perspective Authors
detail.abstract: AI agents are evolving from single-task tools into skills-powered ecosystems with autonomous decision-making capabilities. Agent Skillsengineering mechanisms that encapsulate complex multi-turn prompt chains into reusable behavioural units using natural language as the carrier-are proliferating through skill stores, open-source communities, and multi-source distribution channels. However, a systematic absence of accountability mechanisms throughout the skill lifecycle constitutes what we term a "responsibility vacuum." Based on a cross-platform audit of five mainstream agent platforms encompassing 2,600+ skills, this study found that governance deficiency rates under Wieringa's (2020) four-dimensional algorithmic accountability framework approach or reach 100% across all platforms. Structural analysis of the AgentSkills.io specification reveals the root cause: the specification comprehensively defines functional interfaces while containing zero governance fields. Drawing on the Pacing Problem theory (Marchant et al., 2011), Collingridge's Dilemma (1980), and Anticipatory Governance (Guston, 2014), this paper constructs a "lag diagnosis-risk characterisation-anticipatory response" three-layer analytical framework. An official HKCERT security report (March 2026) documenting actual attack events confirms that this governance vacuum has evolved from theoretical risk to real-world security threat. Adopting a Design Science Research approach, this study develops the "Responsibility Shield" conceptual prototype and R-Skills governance standard, exploring a technically feasible pathway for embedding responsibility tracing mechanisms before the Collingridge window closes. We further introduce the theoretical concept of constitutive blindness-the structural invisibility of governance concerns caused by the ontological closure of functional interoperability standards-to explain why governance gaps are not merely temporal lags but deep-seated exclusion effects. Contributions include systematic conceptualisation of the responsibility vacuum, causal explanation through governance lag theory, identification of the critical intervention window, and an anticipatory governance research agenda for emerging agent skill ecosystems.

detail.abstract:
This Study examines music creators' rights within the EU's legislative framework, focusing on copyright harmonisation and its effects on fairness in the EU digital music market. It provides a comprehensive analysis of challenges facing music creators, covering the topics of Fair MusE's Work Package 2 ("Assessing the Role of Regulation"). 

Part I investigates the rights of composers, performers and record producers under EU law, including their scope as established in EU case law (Chapter 2). It addresses the trade-off between rightholders' protection and users' rights, including provisions on transformative uses, text-and-data mining, and AI (Chapter 3). Drawing on desk and empirical research across 10 EU Member States (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal and Spain), the Study analyses the principle of fair and transparent remuneration under Directive 2019/790 (Chapter 4), examining music licensing trends and contractual practices around composers' and performers' rights to access platform profit data. 

Part II focuses on national implementations of Article 17 of Directive 2019/790 in the same 10 countries. Departing from platform neutrality and the safe harbour of Article 14 of Directive 2000/31, Article 17 establishes a new copyright liability regime for Online Content-Sharing Service Providers (OCSSPs). The Study reviews the provision's origins, the controversies it raised regarding digital enforcement versus fundamental rights (freedom of expression, business freedom), and the CJEU's assessment of these concerns (Chapter 5). Chapter 6 compares national transpositions, examines the industry's response, and explores how rightholders are exercising rights - individually or collectively - and structuring data to support claims against social media platforms. 

Part III analyses national implementations of Directive 2014/26 on collective rights management. Chapter 7 assesses whether EU rules have reduced transaction costs and ensured proportionate remuneration across music industry value chains, examining the roles of Collective Management Organisations (CMOs) and Independent Management Entities (IMEs). It finds that by granting rightholders freedom to choose how to license their works, the Directive spurred repertoire fragmentation in multi-territorial licensing, increasing the number of licences digital music services must obtain from CMOs, publisher hubs and IMEs. Uncertainty around IMEs' obligations adds further complexity, particularly in Italy and Spain. Chapter 8 shows how repertoire fragmentation has complicated the alignment of publishing and recording rights, highlighting the urgent need for robust, interoperable data management infrastructure. Without it, granular and transparent remuneration remains impossible. The Study reviews past integration efforts - including the failed Global Repertoire Database - and analyses transparency obligations for CMOs and online platforms across the 10 countries, finding that greater integration of repertoire data, metadata, and usage reports is essential for equitable revenue distribution. 

The Conclusion (Chapter 9) summarises key findings and presents policy recommendations to inform Fair MusE's "Music Copyright Infrastructure" and the "White Paper on Fairness in Europe's Music Ecosystems".

detail.abstract: This paper compares four classes of NAT traversal mechanism for embedded peer-to-peer (P2P) messaging applications on mobile platforms: classical STUN/TURN/ICE (WebRTC style), libp2p with Distributed Hash Table (DHT) discovery and Direct Connection Upgrade Through Relay (DCUtR), cryptographically-addressed overlay routing of the Yggdrasil class, and Matrix-tailored overlay routing as implemented by Pinecone (matrix.org research). The design analysis is grounded in an independent implementation of an embedded Matrix homeserver stack on mobile, built via gomobile bind around forks of Dendrite (Matrix homeserver in Go) and Pinecone (overlay router). The core claim is that overlay routing transfers complexity from per-connection NAT negotiation to per-network bootstrap and relay infrastructure, making it well-suited for privacy-oriented mobile messaging but unsuitable for browser-based real-time communications. Initial measurements on iPhone 16 Pro Max during a 30-minute test indicate 6 MB resident memory and 0.1% per hour battery consumption for the combined embedded Matrix and Pinecone routing stack. Release builds of the Android .aar artifact range from 35 to 40 MB. Open challenges are stated explicitly: operating under carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT), unverified cross-network connectivity in real mobile networks, invite-flow instability in Matrix federation over overlay routing, and platform-specific background execution limits. The paper is intended as a reproducible design reference for engineers facing similar architectural choices.

detail.abstract: AI Availability extends brand-science accounts of mental and physical availability into AI-mediated discovery, and its measurement programme builds the construct one component at a time. Presence shipped as the first component; Consistency, the stability of a brand's presence across a model panel, is the candidate second. This paper pre-registers and tests the natural operationalization: the coefficient of variation of cross-model recall, mapped to a bounded consistency score. Under a locked protocol applied to three anchored substrates, the instrument fails its pre-registered independence criterion. Consistency correlates with Presence at pooled |𝜌| = 0.77, above the 0.50 ceiling and positive in every substrate. The failure traces to a mechanical identity: at the recall counts language models return, dispersion follows the Poisson relation in which the standard deviation scales with the square root of the mean, so the coefficient of variation approximates the reciprocal of the square root of the mean and reparametrizes presence level rather than isolating a distinct construct. A secondary result documents a recognition-recall gap that leaves consistency undefined for recognized-but-unrecalled brands, concentrated among prestige labels. Per the pre-registered rule, the instrument is not adopted, and the paper specifies the mean-independence requirement any replacement must satisfy.

title: Beyond AI-assisted Writing: Distributed Collaborative Cognition in Interdisciplinary Policy Research A Methodological Reflection on Recursive Human-AI Knowledge Formation

detail.title: Beyond AI-assisted Writing: Distributed Collaborative Cognition in Interdisciplinary Policy Research A Methodological Reflection on Recursive Human-AI Knowledge Formation
detail.abstract:
This paper reflects on the research process used in the development of Taiwan Beyond War, an interdisciplinary working paper series examining governance, population displacement, legal identity, and regional order under Chinese integration scenarios. 

The purpose of this reflection is not to claim autonomous AI authorship, nor to propose a strictly reproducible research methodology, but to document how large-scale interdisciplinary analysis can emerge from differentiated collaboration between human judgment and multiple generative AI systems.

 The process revealed that different generative AI systems exhibited partially distinct cognitive tendencies. ChatGPT repeatedly demonstrated strength in conceptual expansion, interdisciplinary abstraction, exploratory reframing, and adversarial critique, while Claude demonstrated strength in extended coherence, stylistic stability, structural integration, and document-level consistency. 

The process also revealed important limitations in single-model cognition. Extended interaction within a single generative system tended toward self-reinforcing abstraction, rhetorical closure, and conceptual drift. Recursive dialogue across models introduced competing cognitive styles and alternative analytical pressures, partially counteracting these tendencies. 

The resulting workflow differed substantially from conventional AI-assisted writing. Rather than functioning as a linear drafting procedure, the process developed into a recursive cognitive environment in which expansion, critique, restructuring, and stabilization continuously interacted. 

This paper argues that distributed collaborative cognition — a form of human–AI collaborative inquiry that this paper both describes and exemplifies — represents a potentially replicable approach to interdisciplinary policy research. The framework is proposed as a foundation for future practice in any research environment where no single researcher can easily maintain simultaneous expertise across multiple specialized domains. This paper provides the methodological foundation for the accompanying Taiwan research project and policy essay.

detail.abstract: This article analyzes Yellow Card (T) Ltd v. Nyamwero Michael Nyamwero (HC Commercial Case No. 12171 of 2024), a landmark Tanzanian case addressing the legal status of cryptocurrency transactions in a jurisdiction lacking a formal regulatory framework. The dispute arose from the alleged misappropriation of funds by a former company director and his subsequent breach of a settlement agreement requiring repayment. The court held in favor of the plaintiff, concluding that although cryptocurrency activities remain unregulated in Tanzania, they are not inherently illegal. Accordingly, the court enforced the settlement agreement, affirming that contracts involving digital assets are valid and binding when they satisfy ordinary principles of contract law.   The article argues that the decision reflects a broader trend toward technological neutrality in legal interpretation, whereby courts apply existing legal doctrines to emerging technologies without requiring explicit legislative authorization. It highlights the case’s significance as a precedent for recognizing digital assets within contract law and its implications for financial regulation, investor confidence, and judicial approaches to innovation. By situating the ruling alongside comparable decisions in the United States, China, and the European Union, the author underscores both the global convergence toward recognizing cryptocurrency-related agreements and the continued need for comprehensive regulatory frameworks to address risks, taxation, and enforcement in digital finance.

detail.title: Bridging Predictions and Interventions: An Integrated Framework for Automated Decision-Systems

publicationDetails.journalName: Columbia Law School, Public Law & Legal Theory Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Automated decision systems (ADS) leverage predictions about individual future outcomes to inform consequential decision-making in organizational settings. Across various settings-including criminal pretrial release, clinical triage, student support, and more-it is often assumed that improved predictive accuracy is the priority consideration in determining better downstream outcomes upon the deployment of ADS. In practice, real-world case studies reveal that this is far from the case: introducing individual predictions into decision-making modifies organizational workflows, assessment, and decision-making processes in ways that require a complete reconsideration of our approach to the design, evaluation, and deployment of ADS. As a result, this Perspective develops an integrated framework for studying ADS in social systems, shifting current priorities from a purely prediction-based paradigm towards an intervention-oriented view that accounts for real-world conditions. Our aim is to improve our understanding of ADS and more meaningfully anticipate its downstream societal and organizational consequences.

title: Neural Model-Applying Network (NeuMAN): A New Model for Computational Cognition

detail.title: Neural Model-Applying Network (NeuMAN): A New Model for Computational Cognition
detail.abstract: NeuMAN represents a new model for computational cognition synthesizing important results across AI, psychology, and neuroscience. NeuMAN is based on three important ideas: (1) neural mechanisms perform all requirements for intelligence without symbolic reasoning on finite sets, thus avoiding exponential matching algorithms; (2) the network reinforces hierarchical abstraction and composition for sensing and acting; and (3) the network uses learned sequences within contextual frames to make predictions, minimize reactions to expected events, and increase responsiveness to high-value information. These systems will exhibit both the automatic and deliberate aspects that Kahneman termed System One (S1) and System Two (S2), respectively. NeuMAN accords with a wide variety of findings in neural and cognitive science and will supersede symbolic reasoning as a foundation for AI and as a model of human intelligence. It will likely become the principal mechanism for engineering intelligent systems. Unfortunately, these agents will manifest biases latent in their training experiences. Society will face major opportunities and challenges in adapting to the plethora of agents that NeuMAN devices will make commonplace.

detail.abstract: Private capital markets have blurred traditional lines in corporate finance, outflanking the company law ban on public offers of securities by private limited companies and the use of the plc form as a hook for tailored requirements. With today's policy focus being on improving access to capital for all companies, the company law ban on public offers has become a hindrance for companies that want to use innovative offer and trading platforms. The illogicality of using plc form rather than trading status or company size for regulatory tailoring has also become more obvious. The multi-layered nature of modern corporate publicness requires a different approach.

title:
The Upstream Diagnostic Gap 
Why Sovereign Debt Assessments Cannot See What Is Failing Beneath them
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
The Upstream Diagnostic Gap 
Why Sovereign Debt Assessments Cannot See What Is Failing Beneath them
detail.abstract: Standard sovereign debt and fiscal diagnostics-including the Debt Management Performance Assessment (DeMPA) and the Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) framework-assess the quality of debt management offices and fiscal institutions. Neither is designed to evaluate the upstream digital platforms on which their outputs depend. This policy brief argues that the resulting diagnostic gap is material, currently unmeasured, and growing in severity as the internal and external contexts of sovereign fiscal management become more complex and more dynamically interconnected. Evidence from a World Bank-documented case in Honduras suggests that the lag between upstream platform failure and formal recognition may extend to four years or more-a period during which fiscal risk accumulates undetected by any standard instrument. Archer's Model of Digital Governance (AMDG), validated across 111 programmes in 58 countries, is presented as a structured upstream complement to existing diagnostics. Four policy recommendations are offered for multilateral lenders, credit rating agencies, finance ministries, and the World Bank and IMF.

detail.abstract: Generative AI has reduced the marginal cost of producing text, summaries, analysis, and recommendations to near zero. This paper argues that the economic consequence is not simply abundance, but a structural shift in where scarcity resides. As synthetic output scales, the bottleneck moves from production to evaluation: the scarce resources are no longer the outputs themselves, but the trust, provenance, domain expertise, accountability, and judgment required to determine whether those outputs are reliable enough to act upon. The paper frames synthetic output as an economic object: a category of informational good defined not only by its content, but by the conditions of its production and the indeterminacy of its quality. Drawing from information economics, signaling theory, institutional economics, trustworthy AI governance, human-in-the-loop machine learning, and emerging concerns in AI-assisted decision systems, it examines how the proliferation of synthetic output changes the economics of decision making in environments where generated outputs are used to support interpretation, recommendation, forecasting, evaluation, or strategic action. This paper is exploratory and conceptual. Its aim is to define the economic problem clearly and to connect that problem to a broader research trajectory on AI-generated response evaluation, output quality control, and human-in-the-loop decision-readiness. The closing argument is simple: synthetic output abundance does not decrease the value of trusted judgment. It increases it.

• balance sheet categories represent unresolved temporal economic residual state
• income statement and statement of cash flows classifications represent projection

• primitive temporal residual states

title: Reconciling Treatment Effects Estimates across Levels of Aggregation
affiliations: McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management, Princeton University,  and University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: Reconciling Treatment Effects Estimates across Levels of Aggregation
detail.abstract: Empirical researchers often estimate treatment effects at different levels of aggregation to address confounding shocks or to detect violations of the stable unit treatment value assumption. Using eight widely used datasets on trade, employment, syndicated loans, patents, and stock holdings, we document that disaggregated data share common properties that complicate comparisons across aggregation levels. We show that, under standard specifications, these properties can lead treatment effect estimates to differ across levels of aggregation even in the absence of shocks or SUTVA violations. These gaps arise mechanically from implicit weighting across levels of aggregation, entry and exit, and Jensen's inequality. We characterize the conditions under which they become quantitatively important and propose simple approaches that are not sensitive to these sources of bias. Using practical examples, we show how aligning estimates across levels of aggregation can help researchers separately identify confounding shocks, spillovers, and extensive-margin changes at little additional cost.

detail.abstract: Moral universalism-applying identical moral standards to strangers and in-groups-is typically measured via costless bystander allocation. We argue such measures capture discretionary benevolence rather than moral behavior under incentive conflict. We propose an incentivized measure of Universalism in Honesty using a constant-sum "mindcheating" game where dishonesty yields personal gain at a counterpart's expense. In a large-scale experiment in China, we find that honesty-based universalism is largely orthogonal to standard altruism-based measures. We uncover a cognitive paradox: higher cognitive capacity predicts universal honesty, yet longer deliberation correlates with greater parochialism. Furthermore, honesty-based universalism is uniquely predicted by historical exposure to Confucian education and strongly correlates with sociopolitical attitudes, including support for free trade and impartial institutions, which altruism-based measures fail to explain. Our findings demonstrate that moral universalism is multidimensional: the breadth of benevolence does not guarantee the strength of integrity.

title: Skewness Managed Portfolios
affiliations: GMO LLC, Hofstra University - Department of Finance and Rowan University - Accounting & Finance

detail.title: Skewness Managed Portfolios
detail.abstract: We show that the returns to many prominent cross-sectional anomalies are driven by a small number of extreme, positively skewed stock returns. Consistent with this, we propose a skewness-managed strategy that predicts ex-ante skewness using firm characteristics and modifies each anomaly portfolio by selecting high-skewness stocks in the long leg and low-skewness stocks in the short leg. Applied to 18 well-known anomalies, the strategy improves returns by an average of 5.45 percentage points, with gains concentrated in periods of economic and financial stress. Sharpe ratios also increase consistently, with an average gain of 0.12. Despite closely tracking the original factors, these skewness-managed portfolios deliver significant alphas even relative to models constructed from the same characteristics, suggesting that modern asset pricing models may systematically overlook higher-order moments.

title: Autonomous Negotiation via Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents: Efficiency, Fairness, and Mechanisms
affiliations: , Fudan University and Fudan University - School of Management

detail.title: Autonomous Negotiation via Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents: Efficiency, Fairness, and Mechanisms
detail.abstract: Business-to-business (B2B) markets power the global economy, yet complex bilateral negotiations often remain slow, fragmented, and inefficient when parties must bargain over multiple issues under private information. Existing market mechanisms rarely solve this tension among efficiency, agility, and privacy. We address this challenge by designing and evaluating an agent-to-agent negotiation framework for multi-issue bilateral exchange. In our setting, autonomous buyer and seller agents hold heterogeneous private preferences and learn adaptive bargaining strategies through self-play reinforcement learning under two-sided incomplete information. The result is striking: near-efficient and fair agreements emerge from decentralized, self-interested interactions without requiring either party to reveal private preferences to the counterparty or a central platform. Across heterogeneous negotiation environments, the agents capture about 91% of the socially optimal surplus in complex multi-issue settings and up to 98% in canonical single-issue benchmarks. We identify two mechanisms behind this performance: interepisode convergence toward reciprocal bargaining strategies and intra-episode inference that helps agents resolve late-stage impasses. We also uncover a counterintuitive boundary condition: payoff observability can undermine, rather than facilitate, cooperation. These findings suggest a core design principle for agentic commerce: privacy preservation and economic efficiency can be complements, not tradeoffs.

title: Interpretive Crystallization: How Loper Bright Changes the Temporal Logic of Administrative Law

detail.title: Interpretive Crystallization: How Loper Bright Changes the Temporal Logic of Administrative Law
detail.abstract: The Supreme Court's decision in Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024) is conventionally understood as a redistribution of interpretive power from agencies to courts. This essay argues that the more significant consequence is temporal: Loper Bright changes the mechanism through which statutory meaning stabilizes over time. The essay introduces the concept of "interpretive crystallization" — the gradual accumulation of judicial decisions that progressively narrows the range of plausible statutory interpretations and produces a body of law substantially more resistant to political reversal than administrative reinterpretation under Chevron. By reframing the post-Chevron debate around temporal stability rather than institutional competition, the essay offers a new analytical lens for understanding the future trajectory of the administrative state.

title: Foreign Direct Investment and Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS): The Case of Latin American & Caribbean Developing Economies
affiliations: Institute of Management Studies, University of Peshawar

detail.title: Foreign Direct Investment and Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS): The Case of Latin American & Caribbean Developing Economies
detail.abstract: The growing share of knowledge-intensive products in international trade and the increasing sensitivity of multinational firms to intellectual property theft make it imperative to analyse the effect of IPR promulgation on their FDI decision. In this perspective the current article gauge the importance of Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) agreement under World Trade Organisation (WTO) in increasing a Latin American & Caribbean (LAC) developing economy's appeal for investors from abroad. Infrastructure and skilled labour availability, market size, macroeconomic stability, economic development and trade liberalisation are also considered. Time invariant phenomena such as access to the sea, regional affiliations/proximities, income groupings and ability to speak one of the international languages, though desirable were not done because fixed effect panel estimation technique does not permit the use of dummy variables. Due to the 2008-2009 recession in the developed economies, the available investment funds withered, making the investors' sceptic apropos the safety of their tangible and intangible property, especially in the developing world, causing a decrease in FDI to these nations in general. However, LAC countries were somewhat resilient and received a steadily increasing flow of foreign investment. Thus, it demands analysing the factors that overcame the overseas investors' scepticism and prompted them to invest in LAC region. By utilising annual data for 28 years that is 1989-2016 from 24 LAC developing nations it is found that infrastructure and human capital availability, macroeconomic stability, economic development, strengthening and worldwide harmonisation of intellectual property right standards through TRIPS positively effects the overseas investor's investment decision. The population used to measure market size is found to be insignificant when tested with other conventional FDI location pull factors. Similarly, liberalisation, consistent with horizontal FDI theory, exerts a significant negative effect on inward FDI.

title: Food for Thought: Inflation Perceptions and Household Heterogeneity
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome and

detail.title: Food for Thought: Inflation Perceptions and Household Heterogeneity
detail.abstract: Perceived inflation in the Euro Area systematically departs from measured HICP inflation. This gap arises because households place disproportionate weight on salient consumption items, especially frequently purchased goods such as food. Since these items also tend to adjust prices more often, they generate inflation signals that are noisier and more volatile than aggregate inflation. At the micro level, households that are more exposed to food in their consumption basket exhibit a stronger response of perceived inflation to an adverse food supply shock. Additionally, stronger inflation perceptions are accompanied by a sharper increase in pessimism regarding consumption attitudes. At the macro level, perceived inflation reacts with more intensity and persistence compared with actual inflation, while retail sales decline. To interpret these results, we develop a HANK framework with non-homothetic preferences and subjective inflation perceptions. The model shows that heterogeneity in consumption baskets and the greater price volatility of salient goods jointly amplify the effects of negative supply shocks affecting those goods, turning food price disturbances into broader and more persistent contractions in economic activity.

title: Low Birthweight and Child Achievement: Does Pre-K Compensate?

detail.title: Low Birthweight and Child Achievement: Does Pre-K Compensate?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study used anonymized secondary data and did not involve direct contact with human participants. Ethical approval was not required under the applicable institutional guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether pre-kindergarten (pre-K) attendance mediates the relationship between low birthweight and children's academic achievement in elementary school. Using the Early Childhood Longitudinal Study, Kindergarten Class of 2010-11 (ECLS-K:2011), a nationally representative sample that tracks children from kindergarten through fifth grade, I estimate a mediation model that combines OLS with heteroskedasticity-based IVs, following Lewbel (2012, 2018). The results confirm that low birthweight exerts a persistent, negative direct effect on standardized reading and math test scores throughout elementary school, with larger penalties for mathematics. The direct effect ranges from approximately-0.21 standard deviations in reading to-0.27 in math, and OLS estimates are systematically downward-biased in absolute value relative to the IV estimates. The estimated indirect effect operating through pre-K participation is consistently small and statistically insignificant, indicating that pre-K does not substantially mediate the birthweight-achievement relationship at the national level. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that the direct effect is substantially larger among low-income families, with IV estimates approaching-0.41 standard deviations, while high-income families show no statistically significant direct effect. Among lowincome households, the indirect effect through pre-K is positive, though imprecisely estimated. These findings suggest that the cognitive consequences of low birthweight are concentrated among disadvantaged children, and that targeted, high-quality early interventions-rather than broadly available pre-K programs-may be necessary to offset them.

title: The Hand-to-Mouth Share Over The Business Cycle

detail.title: The Hand-to-Mouth Share Over The Business Cycle
detail.abstract: This paper constructs a novel quarterly time series of the Hand-to-Mouth (H2M) share for the United States, 1989-2024, by jointly exploiting the Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) and the Consumer Expenditure Survey (CEX). The resulting series reveals that the H2M share is far from constant: it exhibits sizable fluctuations at business-cycle frequency and is markedly countercyclical, rising in downturns and falling in expansions. This countercyclicality holds both unconditionally and conditional on a broad set of demand and supply shocks identified through a Bayesian Proxy-VAR. Furthermore, I show that a canonical Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian (HANK) model, in which the H2M share is naturally endogenous, reproduces this conditional countercyclicality in response to the identified shocks.

title: Corporate Leverage Under a Corner Solution Proposition - When Lenders Say 'No': Supply-Side Constraints on Leverage

detail.title: Corporate Leverage Under a Corner Solution Proposition - When Lenders Say 'No': Supply-Side Constraints on Leverage
detail.abstract:
The Modigliani-Miller theorem implies that, in the presence of corporate taxes and no bankruptcy costs, firms should increase leverage until equity tends to zero. Yet even firms with stable cash flows and low asset betas maintain interior leverage ratios — the Modigliani-Miller leverage paradox. This paper resolves the paradox by showing that competitive, risk-averse lenders rationally impose a strict supply-side leverage ceiling Lmax(βa) that decreases with the systematic risk of the firm’s assets. This ceiling emerges endogenously from the creditor’s mean-variance portfolio optimization problem and constitutes a corner solution on credit supply. It does not require asymmetric information, bankruptcy costs, agency conflicts, or any departure from frictionless Arrow–Debreu conditions (as derived in Proposition 0 and formalized in Appendices A, B and B’).

The model generates the well-documented negative relation between asset beta and leverage through a purely supply-driven channel that is fully consistent with general equilibrium. The Expanded Model (Propositions 11 onward) incorporates, one at a time, the classic frictions of the modern literature — bankruptcy costs, risk anomaly, bond covenants, agency costs, credit rationing, leverage cycles and funding liquidity, heterogeneous beliefs, the leverage ratchet effect, and macroeconomic uncertainties. In every case, these frictions can only reduce equilibrium leverage relative to the lender-imposed ceiling Lmax(βa) never push it above. The supply-side leverage ceiling thus provides a general mechanism that nests many traditional capital structure explanations as special cases.

By focusing on one of the simplest and most observable features of debt markets — that lenders eventually say “no” — this paper proposes a supply-side theory of debt capacity and credit supply constraints that remains inside the general equilibrium benchmark. Most of the literature asks “why doesn’t the firm take on more debt?” and looks to the demand side. We ask a different question: “who would lend to a firm with no equity?” and locate the answer in the creditor’s portfolio optimization problem.

title: The Macroeconomics of Stablecoins
affiliations: Bank for International Settlements (BIS) - Monetary and Economic Department, Deutsche Bundesbank and

detail.title: The Macroeconomics of Stablecoins
detail.abstract: We analyse the macroeconomic impact of stablecoins using a quantitative macroeconomic model. Stablecoins influence the economy through two opposing channels: (i) a bank lending channel, as household demand for stablecoins raises deposit rates, increases bank funding costs, and reduces loan supply; and (ii) a fiscal space channel, as stablecoin issuers' demand for Treasury bills lowers sovereign borrowing costs, expands fiscal space for tax reductions or higher spending. Calibrated to the U.S., the model predicts that widespread stablecoin adoption modestly reduces long-run output, as the bank lending channel outweighs the fiscal space channel. However, the overall long-run impact may shift under alternative scenarios about stablecoin reserve asset regulation, the level of public debt and the strength of foreign demand. Moreover, the fiscal space channel activates more quickly than the bank lending channel, resulting in significantly positive short-term output effects during the transition phase. Additionally, the model suggests a strengthening of monetary policy transmission via the bank lending channel.

title: Ordinal Marginal Preference Theory: A Vector Field Representation
affiliations: National Chengchi University (NCCU) and National Chengchi University (NCCU)

detail.title: Ordinal Marginal Preference Theory: A Vector Field Representation
detail.abstract: This paper examines, within a vector-field framework, the relationship between ordinal Total Utility (TU) theory and Ordinal Inter-Domain Marginal Preference (OIMP) theory, together with the conditions under which each applies. We show that the correspondence between the two frameworks depends critically on the dimensionality and topological structure of the preference vector field. In a two-dimensional commodity space, or more generally in higher-dimensional conservative fields satisfying the relevant integrability conditions, TU and OIMP are linked through standard calculus: one may pass between them by differentiation and integration, implying path independence in utility realization. However, once additive separability is relaxed and the analysis moves into higher-dimensional non-conservative fields, the global total utility function ceases to be well defined, and the correspondence breaks down. In this more general setting, OIMP exhibits broader explanatory scope: it can accommodate path dependence through local marginal-preference vector fields and provides a framework capable of incorporating reference-point effects and complex interactions across goods. We argue that OIMP offers a more flexible mathematical language than the traditional scalar total-utility representation and thereby helps clarify the domain of validity and theoretical boundary of TU theory.

title: Nitrogen dynamics under conservation tillage in sub-humid tropical conditions of Zimbabwe ​
affiliations: Marondera University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Marondera University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Marondera University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, University of the Free State and Marondera University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology

detail.title: Nitrogen dynamics under conservation tillage in sub-humid tropical conditions of Zimbabwe ​
detail.abstract: Nitrogen (N) is an essential macronutrient for plant growth and productivity, but deficient in most Zimbabwean soils and its dynamics under conservation tillage are not well documented. The objective was to determine the effects of fertilizer application on mineral N dynamics and yield of maize (Zea mays L) and soybean (Glycine max (L) Merr) under conservation tillage in sub-humid tropical conditions of North Western Zimbabwe. Soil N mineralization was measured using in-situ incubation of undisturbed soil cores and soil N was determined using the method of extraction with 0.5M K2SO4. Nitrogen in aboveground plant tissue and grain was determined using spectrophotometry after Kjeldhal digestion. Soil N mineralization steadily increased as the growing season progressed and soil mineral N was 6.9% higher under conventional tillage compared to conservation tillage. The effects of mineral fertilizer application on soil N mineralization were highest in mulched plots and lowest in maize monocropping. Similar to N uptake at 5 weeks after planting (wap), grain and stover N uptake were highest when a combination of reduced tillage and mulching practices were used and lowest under conventional tillage. Highest soil N mineralization, maize N uptake, soybean N uptake and grain yield are achievable when all the three practices of conservation agriculture are applied compared with application of one or two practices as currently adopted by smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa. Combining mineral fertilizer application with conservation agriculture results in higher soil N mineralization, N uptake and grain yield when compared with fertilizer application under conventional tillage.

title: Success Begets Success: The Dynamic Treatment Effects of Financial Aid Tournaments

detail.title: Success Begets Success: The Dynamic Treatment Effects of Financial Aid Tournaments
detail.abstract: Financial aid programs in higher education vary widely in design, including how aid is structured and the timing of provision. This paper studies the impact of financial aid provided as a repeated tournament and its dynamic treatment effects. Pooling administrative data that captures 32% of all tertiary students in a single European country, I exploit a relative GPAbased eligibility rule in a regression discontinuity design to estimate the causal impacts of two types of aid: tuition waivers and stipends. Both forms of aid yield large returns; waiver (stipend) eligibility increases graduation rates by 12.4 (6.6) percentage points, and increases student next-semester GPA by 0.38 (0.21) standard deviations. I find a powerful crowding-in effect, where receiving aid in one semester significantly increases the probability of receiving it in the future, driving a substantial portion of the total long-term benefit. Exploring tournament heterogeneity reveals a distinct life-cycle of aid: early-semester awards appear to be most effective, with the effectiveness diminishing in later semesters. Finally, I show that while short-term tournament incentives exhibit dynamic complementarity by maximizing the effort of high-achieving students, the long-term impact on degree attainment is deeply compensatory for lower-achieving students. These findings reveal a dualmargin response: while competitive aid incentivizes academic effort from top performers, its long-term impact operates by retaining and graduating marginal students.

title: Credit Insurance, Bailout and Systemic Risk
affiliations: Ashoka University

detail.title: Credit Insurance, Bailout and Systemic Risk
detail.abstract: This paper highlights a new channel through which too-big-to-fail (TBTF) institutions endogenously arise in the market and create systemic risk. During the crisis of 2008, the regulator used the imperfectly targeted policy of bailing out AIG to save the counterparty banks. I build a model in which anticipation of such a policy incentivizes the banks to make correlated investments ex ante, thus creating systemic risk, and then write underpriced insurance contracts with a single insurance firm, making it endogenously too-big-to-fail. Further, the insurance firm, instead of diversifying its risk, invests in the same industry as the banks. Limiting the size of the insurance firms can mitigate these problems. However, central clearing counterparties cannot mitigate the risk of counterparty default and subsequent bailout.

title: Rising in Smoke: The Spillover Effect of Environmental Hazard on US Household Homeowners Insurance Expenditure
affiliations: Lingnan University

detail.title: Rising in Smoke: The Spillover Effect of Environmental Hazard on US Household Homeowners Insurance Expenditure
detail.abstract: This study examines how wildfire smoke influences homeowners insurance expenditure and the channels through which climate risk information diffuses across U.S. counties. Using a novel dataset of county-level homeowners insurance premiums covering 2,608 U.S. counties from 2014 to 2024, and NOAA’s Hazard Mapping System smoke data, we employ spatial panel regressions with multiple connectivity matrices based on geographical proximity, cross-county migration, and social networks to examine the impact of wildfire smoke on insurance expenditure. We document strong regional spillovers: smoke events in neighboring counties are associated with a 3.38% to 8.85% increase in local insurance premiums. High spatial correlation in insurance premiums amplifies these spillovers. Cross-county migration emerges as a key dynamic learning channel, while social networks and migration serve as complementary mechanisms for transmitting climate risk information. Our findings highlight the importance of incorporating spillovers when assessing climate risk in insurance markets.​

title: Climate Change, Adaptation, and Vineyard Profitability: Evidence from French Viticulture
affiliations: and Bordeaux School of Economics

detail.title: Climate Change, Adaptation, and Vineyard Profitability: Evidence from French Viticulture
detail.abstract: This study exploits spatial heterogeneity in profit responses to temperature to project climate change impacts on French vineyard profitability, explicitly accounting for both historical and potential future adaptation. Using an original farm-level dataset combined with highresolution daily weather data, we first show that profit losses from frost and extreme heat are smaller in regions historically exposed to such conditions, suggesting long-run adaptation. Incorporating this heterogeneity into forward looking simulations, we then find that profitability is expected to decrease overall under climate change, with losses being relatively homogeneous across regions. Yet, allowing for future adaptation-by extrapolating current cross-regional profit responses to future climates-fully offsets these losses at both the national and local levels. Comparing these estimates with those produced by a standard model assuming uniform profit responses further highlights the importance of accounting for both historical and future adaptation when modeling climate change impacts.

title: PSO-LSTM: A Proactive, Reliability-gated Variant of PSO-EECS for WSN Cluster-head Selection
affiliations: Hassan II University, Hassan II University, Hassan II University and  R&D Department at Watt.ma Company

detail.title: PSO-LSTM: A Proactive, Reliability-gated Variant of PSO-EECS for WSN Cluster-head Selection
detail.abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) deployed in real-world settings face heterogeneous operatingconditions in which conventional cluster-head (CH) selection based on instantaneousmetrics cannot anticipate short-term reliability degradation, leading to prematureCH failures and reduced network lifetime. We propose PSO-LSTM, a proactive reliabilitygatedextension of PSO-EECS, in which a lightweight Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)model at the base station predicts short-horizon node failure probabilities from per-nodetemporal signals. These predictions form a set-level reliability score that multiplicativelygates the energy-centric term of the PSO fitness, recovering PSO-EECS behavior understable conditions. Experiments are conducted over 20 paired seeds on a 200-node heterogeneousWSN incorporating six co-occurring heterogeneity factors: energy variability, spatialhotspots, stochastic traffic, retransmission faults, energy harvesting, and asymmetric sinkplacement. Compared with seven bio-inspired baselines, namely PSO with GravitationalSearch Algorithm (PSOGSA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Whale Optimization Algorithm(WOA), Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO), Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO), PSO-EECS, and anablated no-gate variant, PSO-LSTM achieves statistically significant improvements on FirstNode Dead (FND) (Δ ≥ +4.68%, padj ≤ 0.023, δ ≥ +0.761), Last Node Dead (LND)(Δ ≥ +6.21%, padj ≤ 0.001, δ = +1.000), and cumulative throughput (Δ ≥ +2.50%,padj ≤ 0.001, δ = +1.000), while introducing no statistically significant Half Node Dead(HND) degradation (padj ≥ 0.088), confirming the gate’s non-disruptiveness during stablenetwork operation. Ablation analysis confirms that the reliability gate is the key mechanismdriving these improvements.

title: Fragility Without Crises: Reassessing Systemic Instability in Italian Banking, 1890-1973
affiliations: University of Turin

detail.title: Fragility Without Crises: Reassessing Systemic Instability in Italian Banking, 1890-1973
detail.abstract: Does the absence of a crisis imply a stable banking system? This paper argues it does not. Thus, the analysis focuses on "banking fragility" – defined as a deterioration of bank fundamentals – to disentangle salient crises from underlying vulnerability in the Italian banking sector from 1890 to 1973. To achieve this, I construct a novel metric: the Bank Fragility Index (BFI). Using micro-level balance sheet data from the Bank of Italy's Archivio Storico del Credito in Italia (ASCI), the BFI employs fuzzy-set calibration to synthesise fundamental deterioration, proxied by the cross-sectional segmentation of banking profitability. I show that banking crises and fragility intersect during major systemic events but lack a mechanical linkage. Specifically, I identify: (1) a "high finance bias" during the liberal period, when crises were limited to major banks without broader fundamental impairment (1891, 1893, 1907, 1921); (2) recurrent episodes of "fragility without crises" during macroeconomic downturns (1894-1899, 1912, 1927-1929, 1943-1947, 1963-67), with quantitative results for the 1960s cross-validated by archival evidence to reveal a previously overlooked spike in fragility (3) that latent fragility relates to an erosion of operational efficiency, whereas crises during already-fragile regimes are characterised by a significant deleveraging. This perspective links traditional historical narratives of banking crises with recent macro-financial efforts to quantify structural impairment using bank-level data. In doing so, it reveals that the Italian banking sector was fundamentally more fragile over the long run than traditional accounts imply.

title: Does Stronger Trade Secret Protection Benefit Workers? Quasi-Experimental Evidence from China
affiliations: Shandong University at Weihai and The University of Western Australia - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Does Stronger Trade Secret Protection Benefit Workers? Quasi-Experimental Evidence from China
detail.abstract: The consensus that intellectual property protection favors capital owners overlooks a key difference between patents and trade secrets: a patent is a transferable asset owned by the firm, whereas a trade secret is inseparable from the employees who hold it. Exploiting China's staggered National Trade Secret Protection Innovation Pilot Program as a quasi-natural experiment, we apply a difference-in-differences design to A-share listed firms over 2019–2024 and find that stronger trade secret protection significantly raises the firm-level labor income share. The effect works through a residual distribution reconstruction mechanism: stronger protection raises the bargaining power of secret-holding employees, shifting surplus toward labor, while policy-induced excess profits let firms share gains with workers. Ruling out alternatives such as human capital hoarding, we show the benefits accrue mainly to ordinary employees, narrowing the management–worker wage gap. Human-capital-embedded intellectual property can thus be labor-friendly, unlike the capital-biased effects of patents.

title: Resilience Over Efficiency: How COVID-19, Tariffs, and Geopolitical Tensions Are Reshaping Globalization

detail.title: Resilience Over Efficiency: How COVID-19, Tariffs, and Geopolitical Tensions Are Reshaping Globalization
detail.abstract: The late twentieth and early twenty-first century were shaped by an architecture of globalization based on efficiency. States, firms and multilateral institutions sought to organize cross-border production around comparative advantage, just-in-time manufacturing and the relentless minimization of cost. Recent shocks the pandemic, the U.S-China strategic rivalry, the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the re-emerging strength of economic nationalism, have reshaped that calculus such that governments across the advanced industrial world will actively subordinate efficiency, to resilience, security and strategic autonomy in the future. Drawing on recent developments in semiconductor policy, pharmaceutical supply chains, defense industrial re-armament and energy diversification, this paper traces the structural transition from hyper globalization, to what might be termed, a geoeconomic reconfiguration of global production. We contend that globalization is not retreating; it is being reinvented around geopolitical trust, redundancy and friend-shoring and not just cost minimization alone. The future global economy is likely to increasingly be shaped, not by who can produce most cheaply, but by who can be trusted to supply reliably under conditions of strategic stress.

title: Tort Law at the Frontier of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Yale University - Law School

detail.title: Tort Law at the Frontier of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract:
The frontier of contemporary AI development is dominated by AI systems built on foundation models--highly versatile algorithms, trained in the first instance on broad swathes of data, that can function as tools and agents across a wide variety of commercial, social, military and political domains. For the moment, at least, the process of developing and releasing foundation models is subject to anemic formal regulation and haphazard ex ante governance. Until that changes, it is largely the common law of torts - our society's most ancient and general legal mechanism for governing serious risks of physical injury - that will govern the frontier of AI development.

This Article offers an in-depth conceptual, normative, and doctrinal examination of tort liability for foundation model development and release. It provides a qualified defense of the tort of negligence - the common law's broadest and most flexible cause of action - as the principal doctrinal foundation of the tort system's governance of this novel domain. Legal scholarship on AI liability has been quite hostile to negligence. By contrast, this Article argues that the generality and flexibility of the negligence tort - and its greater sensitivity to the externalized benefits of risky activity - render it well-suited to the polymathic and protean functionality of foundation models. Only the tort of negligence has the breadth and flexibility to address the range of important pathways - including internal deployments, inadequate model weight security, targeted entrustments of non-defective models, and open source releases - by which foundation model developers might cause serious harm.

Analyzing the choice between negligence and competing doctrinal regimes does, however, suggest important ways in which common law courts should incrementally develop the law of negligence, in order to properly reflect the risks and capabilities of foundation models. For example, courts should expand the scope of the duty of care in negligence, in order to provide redress when foundation models cause economic or emotional injury by behaving in ways that are closely analogous to serious human wrongdoing (e.g., certain crimes and intentional torts, such as theft, deceit, and outrage).

But the Article's analysis also suggests certain fundamental pathologies of tort liability as a mechanism of AI governance - pathologies that no amount of doctrinal development will adequately cure. In particular, the specter of tort liability can be expected to disincentivize frontier AI developers from investigating and disclosing many of the novel and poorly understood risks that frontier AI development may pose. That is especially disturbing given that our society is relying quite heavily, for its ability to discover and understand these risks, on frontier AI developers themselves. Thus, tort liability is not only inadequate as a mechanism of frontier AI governance; in certain important respects, it is actively perverse, and its perverse effects must be countered by governance institutions of a different kind. Ultimately, a robust regime of ex ante regulation - under which government institutions or credibly neutral third-party experts are empowered to investigate, evaluate, and mitigate the risks of frontier AI development - is urgently required in frontier AI governance.

title: Employee Heat Protection and Corporate Innovation: Evidence from China
affiliations: Renmin University of China - School of Business, Renmin University of China and

detail.title: Employee Heat Protection and Corporate Innovation: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: We examine the impact of employee heat protection mandates on corporate innovation in the context of global warming. In 2012, China introduced a nationwide policy requiring employers to protect workers from extreme heat. Exploiting variation in firms’ exposure to the policy, we find that more exposed firms engage more actively in innovation. Rather than developing technologies aimed at mitigating workers’ exposure to high temperatures, these firms respond to climate transition risks by pursuing transformative innovation, particularly in artificial intelligence and process innovation. The effect is more pronounced among firms with more-capable employees and stronger incentives for transformation. We further document broader impacts of the policy on firm-level outcomes and inventor relocation decisions. Overall, our findings highlight that firms respond to climate transition risks induced by the national heat protection mandates through transformational strategies aimed at reducing their reliance on labor inputs.

title: The Emerging Architecture of Liquidity and Collateral Transformation: How Four Forces Are Converging to Support the T-Bill Market and U.S. Treasury Debt Issuance
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Emerging Architecture of Liquidity and Collateral Transformation: How Four Forces Are Converging to Support the T-Bill Market and U.S. Treasury Debt Issuance
detail.abstract: The U.S. Treasury market benefits from a deep and diversified buyer base, but debt issuance has expanded at a pace that exceeds the organic capacity of even well-established channels-including domestic institutional demand, foreign official holdings, and bank deposit growth-driving structural reliance on market-based intermediaries. This paper synthesizes four independent developments that, together, expand the effective demand base for Treasuries-especially the T-Bill market: (i) bank capital/liquidity reforms that lower the cost of holding bills; (ii) collateral transformation and tokenized settlement rails that enable 24/7 mobility and real-time margin; (iii) cleared and sponsored repo that open centrally-netted access for buy-side participants; and (iv) a structural bid from regulated stablecoin reserves concentrated in short-dated paper. Using official publications and infrastructure data (Federal Register, TBAC, SEC, DTCC/FICC dashboards, BIS, Fed FEDS Notes), this paper documents rising front-end capacity and maps a correlated-fragility pathway in which stablecoin redemptions, MMF outflows, and margin spikes converge on bills. The analysis surfaces policy questions around the adequacy of existing monitoring frameworks, stablecoin reserve disclosure standards, tokenized collateral data access, and stress-testing coverage of cross-channel convergence scenarios. The contribution is a cross-silo synthesis-showing how these forces are multiplicative, not additive-combined with actionable monitoring and an empirically grounded, falsifiable thesis.

title: A Stochastic Ranking and Allocation Framework for Dependent Performance Measures
affiliations: , Universidad de Alicante, Westminster Business School, University of Westminster and Universidad Pablo de Olavide

detail.title: A Stochastic Ranking and Allocation Framework for Dependent Performance Measures

contentType.other: Original research article submitted to journal

detail.abstract: We develop a distribution-based framework for ranking …nancial assets when performance measures are estimated with uncertainty and are statistically dependent across assets. The method transforms pairwise comparisons of estimated performance measures into domination probabilities, which de…ne a stochastic matrix whose Perron-Frobenius eigenvector provides a complete ranking and, after normalization, a long-only eigenportfolio. For Sharpe ratio estimators, we initially derive closed-form domination probabilities from their joint asymptotic distribution under temporally independent and identically distributed multivariate returns. The associated covariance matrix incorporates correlations, coskewness, and cokurtosis. We further extend the framework to serially dependent returns, to alternative performance measures, including the modi…ed Sharpe ratio and the VaR ratio, and to conditional and …nite-sample Edgeworth-corrected domination probabilities. An empirical application to S&P 500 constituents shows that the proposed eigenportfolio generally outperforms Sharpe ratio benchmarks across di¤erent frequencies. Block-bootstrap evidence supports the robustness of the selection and performance results.

title: Epeditor: A Scalable Platform for Large-ensemble Building Energy Simulation Enabling Agent-Assisted Automation
affiliations: Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University - Department of Building Science and Technology

detail.title: Epeditor: A Scalable Platform for Large-ensemble Building Energy Simulation Enabling Agent-Assisted Automation
detail.abstract: The data scale of energy simulation keeps increasing, particularly in urban building energy modeling (UBEM) and uncertainty analysis, where thousands of EnergyPlus runs are often required to explore complex parameter spaces and building variability. To simplify these data-intensive workflows, recent studies have introduced AI agents for end-to-end simulation tasks. However, in practice, both AI-assisted and conventional batch workflows remain constrained by hallucination-induced search bias, inefficient large-ensemble simulation execution, and cumbersome data processing. To address these problems, this study introduces Epeditor, a cloud-deployable simulation infrastructure for large-ensemble building energy analysis for both AI and human users. It combines three improvements on current workflows: a knowledge-assisted parameterization with more accurate and stable field searching in IDF files; a simulator that improves parallel execution efficiency through Operation-System-Level deployment; and a data management system that enables memory-safe aggregation of large simulation input and outputs. The packaged Agent Skill allows AI agents to execute fully automated dataset generation, batch simulation, surrogate modeling, and interpretation through an auditable workflow. Epeditor is evaluated through a systematical agent benchmarks with metrics for Artificial General Intelligence, and two case studies were introduced to show the ability in research and design practices including an AI-assisted surrogate-modeling case, and design-studio practices. The pipeline exhibits 99.98% robustness in IDF generation, up to four-fold acceleration in high-parallel simulation, and 76.28 (F1) in IDF fields inference. These findings indicate that Epeditor can lower the technical and computational barriers of large-ensemble EnergyPlus simulation, supporting more accessible, reproducible, and AI-ready building energy analysis.

title: Concept Programming for Dependable AI

detail.title: Concept Programming for Dependable AI
detail.abstract: Large language models deployed in critical systems today have no principled method for instilling specified behavioral concepts, whether explicit safety constraints, cultural values, professional norms, or governance principles, that generalize dependably across novel contexts. Such systems are termed Language-Grounded Neural Systems (LGNS) throughout this paper. Methods used to date train what to avoid rather than what to embody, leaving hidden values to emerge unpredictably from pretraining and making dependable behavior impossible to certify or verify. Concept Programming trains each concept as a named positive attractor in the model's neural state space. Concepts that mark prohibitions are paired with blocking responses. Concepts that mark obligations are paired with required action responses. Concepts that embody values shape inference and judgment directly. Each type uses the same training mechanism: instances sampled from the empirical frequency distribution of the concept's semantic case frame, activating the concept's attractor across its full basin. Three controlled experiments on a freely available 3-billion-parameter local model establish the method empirically. Experiment 1 shows that positive concept training achieves 94.4% adherence on governance safety constraints versus 77.8% for punishment-analog training and 47.2% for untrained control, with 100% transfer to novel domains not seen in training. Experiment 2 shows that CP instills cultural value manifolds producing tradition-consistent reasoning on the five canonical moral psychology anchor cases in the published literature; the Buddhist-trained condition achieves a perfect score where the 2 untrained control scores 40%. Experiment 3 characterizes the learning curve and introduces a governance-adapted signal detection framework showing that CP reduced the miss rate from 100% in the untrained control to 19-25% within 200 training cases, with both trained conditions showing a false alarm rate of 42-46% versus 94% in control. The entire experimental program runs on a consumer laptop at negligible cost. CP opens every domain of human activity to more dependable LGNS-based systems and defines a research program as broad as the range of human concepts AI systems will need to embody.

title: Large Zombies, Small Victims: Evidence on Congestion Effects from Population-Level Data
affiliations: The Bank of Korea

detail.title: Large Zombies, Small Victims: Evidence on Congestion Effects from Population-Level Data

keywords.keywords: Zombie firms; Misallocation; Congestion effects; Firm dynamics; Productivity; Firm exit; Private firms

detail.abstract:
Most studies on zombie firms focus on listed firms—which account for only a small fraction of the firm population—largely because of limited access to data on private firms. Using a novel dataset that covers virtually the entire universe of firms in Korea, this study provides new evidence on the extent of zombification in the overall economy, with particular emphasis on private firms, where systematic evidence has been scarce.

We show that the aggregate share of assets and financial liabilities held by zombie firms is driven by externally audited, and thus larger firms, while the economic presence of private zombies remains limited and stable over time. Consistent with the existing literature, we find economically meaningful congestion effects of zombie firms on healthier firms. Higher zombie prevalence is associated with lower investment, employment, productivity, and profitability among non-zombie firms, and these effects persist over time. The adverse spillovers are substantially stronger for smaller firms and for firms operating in non-tradable sectors. These effects are particularly pronounced for investment and employment outcomes, with the heterogeneity being especially strong among private firms. We further show that the exit of zombie firms can generate non-trivial gains in aggregate productivity and value added, while acknowledging that such reallocation may involve distributional trade-offs across firms, workers, and creditors.

Overall, the findings suggest that the primary economic cost of zombification lies not in its prevalence among small firms, but in the disproportionate burden that zombie congestion imposes on smaller firms. This underscores the importance of policies that facilitate corporate restructuring and timely firm exit, while limiting incentives for inefficient credit continuation.

title: Green Investment Intentions among Eurozone SMEs: Financing Climate Adaptation and Mitigation across Heterogeneous Institutional Contexts

detail.abstract: This paper examines climate investment behaviour among Eurozone SMEs, distinguishing between current investment, planned investment, and no engagement using multinomial modelling. It provides novel evidence that adaptation and mitigation are strongly interconnected, with engagement in one domain powerfully predicting the other. The analysis reveals substantial crosscountry heterogeneity driven by institutional context, policy design, and implementation depth. A key finding is the large "intention-action gap," where many firms plan investment but face barriers such as finance and information constraints. The study advances methodological approaches and highlights the need for integrated policy frameworks that target both enabling conditions and disengaged firms

title: Deciphering the Drivers of Price-Labor Value Vector Proximity in Empirical Studies
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Amherst and University of Massachusetts Amherst

detail.title: Deciphering the Drivers of Price-Labor Value Vector Proximity in Empirical Studies
detail.abstract: In the tradition of Classical Political Economy, empirical studies of labor values and prices ask whether labor-value vectors are close to observed market-price vectors. This paper examines the mechanisms that generate such proximity in input-output systems by uncovering the structural features of the linear production system determining the relevant distance. We use the recent critique of Shaikh-style price-value comparisons by Sabatino (2026) as a springboard for this analysis, by deciphering the results she obtains from different artificial datasets. The central result is that, under the direct-price construction examined here, the distance is governed by the dispersion of reciprocal vertically integrated labor coefficients. This shifts attention to the determinants of the vector of vertically integrated labor coefficients: the dispersion of the direct labor vector, the column structure of the Leontief inverse, and the spectral radius of the input-output matrix. The analysis shows that low market price-labor value distance can arise from identifiable structural mechanisms within the production system.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: This paper studies how developing economies should design energy supply chains when renewable infrastructure decisions are shaped by binding operational frictions. We identify three frictions that are prevalent in resource-constrained environments: financial frictions that limit investment capacity, infrastructure frictions that create transmission losses, and supply chain frictions that generate trade-offs between inbound logistics and outbound energy delivery. Methodology/results: We develop a stylized dynamic model that captures endogenous investment capacity, technology heterogeneity, and spatial tradeoffs in hybrid renewable energy supply chains. The model reveals three mechanisms. First, financial frictions induce technology sequencing: fastdeployable technologies are preferred in early stages, while more stable but capital-intensive technologies become attractive as economic capacity expands. Second, infrastructure and logistics frictions induce spatial reconfiguration, shifting optimal biomass facility locations from resource-proximate to demandproximate regions as demand and GDP grow. Third, energy supply chain investments generate an endogenous amplification mechanism by reducing shortages, increasing economic output, and expanding future investment capacity. We then validate these mechanisms using a large-scale multi-period optimization model calibrated to Pakistan, a developing economy facing severe energy shortages and infrastructure constraints. The numerical results show how supply chain design can eliminate energy deficits while supporting economic growth. Managerial implications: The findings provide policymakers and infrastructure planners with mechanism-based guidance for sequencing renewable investments, configuring spatial networks, and designing energy supply chains as growth-enabling systems. By linking development frictions to technology sequencing, spatial reconfiguration, and endogenous investment amplification, and validating these mechanisms in a resource-constrained economy, this paper extends supply chain design theory and contributes to the emerging theory of Development Operations Management.

title: The Effect of Sectoral Diversification on Return and Risk in Portfolio Management: An Application in Borsa Istanbul

detail.title: The Effect of Sectoral Diversification on Return and Risk in Portfolio Management: An Application in Borsa Istanbul
detail.abstract: This paper investigates sectoral diversification within Borsa Istanbul, aiming to elucidate its impact on portfolio risk and return dynamics. Spanning the timeframe from 2020 to 2022, the study meticulously analyzes stocks from pivotal sectors, including banking, energy, and iron and steel. Employing a robust methodology, the research harnesses Monte Carlo simulations to generate many hypothetical portfolios, subsequently evaluating them on the Efficient Frontier to identify optimal risk-return trade-offs. Key performance metrics, such as the Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, and Maximum Drawdown, further enrich the analysis, providing a granular view of portfolio behaviors. The significance of this study lies in its bridging of theoretical constructs of diversification with the tangible realities of an emerging market like Borsa Istanbul. Our main findings underscore the potential benefits of sectoral diversification while highlighting the complexities inherent in portfolio construction. The insights gleaned offer valuable guidance for investors, emphasizing the delicate balance between risk mitigation and return optimization in a diversified portfolio.

title: Still Can’t Tell:  A Close Replication of “Fooled Twice: People Cannot Detect Deepfakes But Think They Can”
